reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism underlying maze navigation involves two interdependent processes: mnemonic encoding and perceptual enhancement. Mnemonic-perceptual inference integrates learned path knowledge with sensory input to guide decisions. This integration is modeled as a Bayesian update where prior beliefs about path structure are refined by new perceptual evidence. Multiple track equivalence introduces stochasticity into decision-making when multiple paths lead to the same outcome, reflecting a form of exploratory behavior driven by symmetry-breaking expectations. Perceptual salience bias further modulates this process by amplifying certain environmental features, thereby shaping both memory formation and choice behavior. These primitives collectively define a dynamic system where cognition emerges from the interaction between memory, perception, and behavioral flexibility.
